papers.title: Tensile and fatigue properties of additively manufactured titanium alloy: Effects of heat treatment and surface processing
papers.abstract: Titanium alloy has been regarded as one of the most demandable and potential materials in the additive manufacturing (AM) community due to its good printability and extensive applications. While the durability and ductility of the as-built titanium alloy specimens were markedly lower than the forgings due to the rough surfaces, acicular martensite structure and high stress state. Here, heat treatment and surface treatment (i.e., shot blasting and machining) were performed on the laser powder bed fused (LPBF) Ti-6Al-4V specimens and forging counterparts to investigate the effects of surface roughness and microstructure on the tensile and fatigue properties. The results indicated that the tensile and fatigue strength were greatly improved after surface treatment, and fatigue limits was further improved after heat treatment. The optimized combination of heat treatment and surface processing provides reliable strategy guidance for the mechanical property improvement of LPBF-produced Ti-6Al-4V alloy.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the tensile and fatigue properties of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V to match those of wrought counterparts.
summary_en.method: Heat treatment and surface processing (shot blasting and machining) were applied to LPBF Ti-6Al-4V specimens, followed by tensile and fatigue testing.
summary_en.result: Surface processing greatly enhanced strength and fatigue limit, which was further improved by subsequent heat treatment.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical tests (tensile and fatigue) comparing as-built, heat-treated, and surface-processed conditions.

papers.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of additively enhanced titanium alloy lightweight high-speed motor shaft
papers.abstract: Abstract High-speed motor shafts are subjected to immense centrifugal forces and demand extremely high dynamic balancing precision. Titanium alloys, characterized by their high specific strength, excellent fatigue resistance, and the design freedom enabled by additive manufacturing, present an ideal material choice for the shaft. Numerical simulation and design are employed to ensure the operational reliability and structural stability of the Titanium alloy shaft under high-speed conditions. Based on the laser cladding technology, a multi-layer laser additive manufacturing process was developed to perform the deposition process on a titanium alloy motor shaft. With the assistance of Al-based high-performance metal powder, this study presents the successful fabrication of a high-performance Al-based composite strengthened coating on Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) titanium alloy motor shaft using laser additive manufacturing. The coating exhibited significantly enhanced mechanical properties compared to the TC4 substrate; microhardness increased from 320 HV to 530-610 HV. Wear tests revealed a substantially reduced friction coefficient compared to the TC4. These results demonstrate that laser additive manufacturing is a viable method for producing the titanium alloy lightweight high-speed motor shaft.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文研究的是Ti-6Al-4V基体上的激光熔覆涂层，而非基体本身的力学或疲劳性能，与方向关注的Ti-6Al-4V增材制造力学性能不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper is about a laser-cladded Al-based composite coating on Ti-6Al-4V, not about the mechanical or fatigue behavior of the base Ti-6Al-4V material itself.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the mechanical properties and wear resistance of high-speed motor shafts.
summary_en.method: An Al-based composite coating was deposited on a Ti-6Al-4V motor shaft using laser cladding additive manufacturing.
summary_en.result: The coating achieved a microhardness increase from 320 HV to 530-610 HV and a significantly reduced friction coefficient compared to the substrate.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microhardness measurements and wear tests.

papers.title: Comparative analysis between traditional topology optimization and lattice structure optimization for additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Structural weight reduction is gaining significance as engineering applications seek to increase the strength-to-weight ratio in their designs. Both lattice structures and topology optimization provide different avenues for achieving weight reduction in mechanical systems. However, comparisons between these methods are rarely conducted when both are subject to the same constraints. A controlled numerical comparison of six lattice geometries, three strut-based (BCC, FCC, Graph-Diamond) and three TPMS-based (Gyroid, Schwarz, Diamond), with a single topology optimized solid was undertaken, all constrained within a design volume of 113 × 20 × 20 mm3 and to the same total mass of approximately 60g of Ti-6Al-4V. Convergence of mesh size was investigated for each structure, and all models were subjected to identical tensile boundary conditions using linear elastic finite element analysis. The topology optimization process used a compliance-minimizing formulation, with the design load selected based on the maximum tensile capacity observed among the lattice specimens.The results clearly indicate that the internal geometry of each of the structures has a direct effect on tensile behaviour. The strut-based lattices have shown significant bending effects and rapid stress localization, leading to failure loads ranging from approximately 7 kN to 20 kN. The TPMS-based geometries have provided a more even distribution of stress and increased capacity compared to the strut-based geometries, with the TPMS "Diamond" geometry capable of supporting loads up to approximately 33.5 kN before approaching the yield strength of the material. The topology-optimized solid had superior tensile properties to all of the lattice geometries, supporting elastic deformation loads of up to 82.5 kN - nearly twice the capacity of the strongest lattice structure, despite being subject to the same total mass constraint. The data demonstrate that the presence of continuous and unbroken load paths can provide a significant mechanical advantage when subjected to tensile loading, and highlight the importance of optimizing geometries in order to produce optimal designs for components to be produced through additive manufacturing.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了Ti-6Al-4V材料的点阵结构与拓扑优化对比，但未涉及任何股骨柄或骨科植入物设计，与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not study a femoral/hip stem or any orthopaedic implant structure; it uses a generic tensile specimen and lacks biomechanical context, stress shielding, or implant-specific loading.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较拓扑优化与点阵结构在减重设计中的力学性能差异。
summary_zh.method: 对六种点阵（BCC、FCC、Graph-Diamond、Gyroid、Schwarz、Diamond）与一种拓扑优化实体进行有限元拉伸对比。
summary_zh.result: 拓扑优化实体承载能力最强（82.5 kN），TPMS Diamond点阵次之（33.5 kN），而支柱类点阵因应力集中性能较差。
summary_zh.validation: 仅有限元分析，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the mechanical performance of topology-optimized solid versus various lattice structures under tensile loading for weight reduction.
summary_en.method: A controlled numerical comparison of six lattice geometries (three strut-based, three TPMS-based) and one topology-optimized solid, all with identical mass and volume, using linear elastic FEA with Ti-6Al-4V material.
summary_en.result: The topology-optimized solid exhibited the highest load capacity (82.5 kN), followed by the TPMS Diamond (33.5 kN), while strut-based lattices showed significant bending and stress localization leading to lower capacities (7-20 kN).
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmark with mesh convergence study, no experimental validation.

papers.title: Experimental investigation of the fatigue performance of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy subjected to shot peening
papers.abstract: Abstract This work systematically investigates the fatigue behavior of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy plates subjected to shot peening under five different intensity levels. Fatigue tests were conducted, and the detailed fatigue rating (DFR) was calculated to quantify fatigue improvement. The results show that shot peening significantly enhances fatigue resistance, with a maximum DFR gain of 48.50%. As the peening intensity increases, the fatigue performance first improves and then declines, indicating that an intermediate peening intensity provides the optimal enhancement. These findings provide experimental support for selecting appropriate shot peening parameters in engineering applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了喷丸处理对Ti-6Al-4V疲劳性能的影响，但未明确为增材制造材料，相关方法可转移至增材制造后处理评估。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not specify the manufacturing route; it likely uses wrought Ti-6Al-4V, not additive-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V, thus it lacks direct relevance to AM post-processing.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究不同喷丸强度对Ti-6Al-4V疲劳性能的影响规律。
summary_zh.method: 对Ti-6Al-4V板材进行五种强度喷丸处理，开展疲劳试验并计算细节疲劳额定值。
summary_zh.result: 喷丸显著提升疲劳性能，中等强度时增益最大达48.50%，过高或过低均使增益下降。
summary_zh.validation: 通过不同喷丸强度下的疲劳试验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how shot peening intensity affects the fatigue performance of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy.
summary_en.method: Fatigue tests were conducted on Ti-6Al-4V plates subjected to five different shot peening intensities, and the detail fatigue rating (DFR) was calculated to quantify improvement.
summary_en.result: Shot peening significantly enhances fatigue resistance, with a maximum DFR gain of 48.50%; an intermediate peening intensity yields the optimal improvement.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue testing with multiple intensity levels.
